Uma exploradora, uma missão e um universo de possibilidades! 🌌

Sou uma participante apaixonada por ciência, tecnologia, inovação e exploração espacial. Nesta jornada do NASA Space Apps Challenge, encaro o desafio de desenvolver um simulador de missão espacial para astronautas juniores, transformando conhecimento em experiências interativas e educativa.

✨ Explorando ideias. Criando possibilidades. Inspirando futuros astronautas!
summary:
Lunar Mission: Junior, developed by the SOLO COSMOS team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, is an educational and interactive simulator designed for children aged 7 to 12. The project aims to introduce young learners to the challenges of space exploration through an experience that combines science, technology, engineering, and fun.

In the game, players take on the role of commanders of a lunar base located at the Moon’s South Pole. Their mission is to ensure the survival of a team of astronauts for seven days. To achieve this, they must manage four essential resources: life support, energy, radiation protection, and food.

Throughout the mission, players face situations such as solar alerts, power failures, communication difficulties, and challenges involving food production. Every decision brings advantages and consequences, helping players understand the challenges and limitations of surviving in space.

The project’s main strength is its ability to turn scientific concepts into practical and accessible challenges, encouraging critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making. The proposal also includes the use of NASA’s open scientific data and research, particularly from the DONKI and OSDR repositories, as well as information from the Artemis program.

More than just a game, Lunar Mission: Junior aims to spark scientific curiosity, promote STEM learning, and inspire a new generation of space explorers.
details:
LUNAR MISSION: JUNIOR — Your Mission. Your Decisions. Your Moon!

Team: SOLO COSMOS

Lunar Mission: Junior is an interactive educational game designed for children aged 7 to 12, inspired by the challenges of human exploration of the Moon. The project transforms the experience of managing a lunar research base into an engaging learning adventure, where players become commanders responsible for the survival of a team of astronauts during a seven-day mission at the Moon's South Pole.

Throughout the game, players face unexpected situations involving solar activity, radiation risks, energy shortages, lunar dust, food production, and communication difficulties. To overcome these challenges, they must manage four essential resources: life support, energy, radiation protection, and food supply. Each decision has consequences, changing resource levels and influencing the mission's outcome. Players can achieve mission success, partial success, or failure, encouraging experimentation, strategic thinking, and learning from mistakes.

The project offers an accessible and playful way to introduce complex scientific and technological concepts to young learners. Its educational benefits include developing critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making, resource management, scientific curiosity, and an understanding of the challenges astronauts face in space. Interactive tutorials, a friendly astronaut guide, educational challenges, a science quiz, achievements, and mission feedback make learning more engaging and meaningful.

Our intended impact is to inspire children to explore science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), while encouraging interest in astronomy and future space exploration. We also aim to demonstrate that scientific learning can begin at an early age through creativity, interaction, and practical challenges. The game is designed to make space science more accessible, exciting, and understandable for children.

The project is being developed as a browser-based application using Lovable, an AI-powered development platform. Its web application architecture uses modern technologies such as React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. The game also incorporates interactive interfaces, animations, sound effects, resource management systems, and browser-based local storage to save player progress. NASA's publicly available scientific resources, including DONKI, OSDR, and Artemis educational materials, serve as references for the scientific concepts presented. Game resource values and mission scenarios are educational simulations, not real-time measurements or operational NASA data.

The creative aspect of Lunar Mission: Junior is the combination of space exploration, interactive storytelling, and strategic resource management in a child-friendly game. Instead of simply presenting scientific information, the project allows children to experience the consequences of decisions similar to those faced by space mission teams. Every choice becomes an opportunity to understand how science and engineering work together.

During the design process, we considered the target audience's age, accessibility, intuitive navigation, visual appeal, educational value, scientific accuracy, and the balance between entertainment and learning. We also considered the importance of presenting realistic space exploration challenges without making the experience too complex for children.

Lunar Mission: Junior is more than a game: it is an invitation to imagine, explore, learn, and become part of the next generation of space explorers.

SOLO COSMOS — One Explorer. One Mission. A Universe of Possibilities.
